title: PAC-3 Edge Will Be The Most Capable Patriot Interceptor Ever
summary: The new interceptor will sit at the top of the Patriot missile family and promises more range, altitude, and maneuverability against rapidly-developing threats. The post PAC-3 Edge Will Be The Most Capable Patriot Interceptor Ever appeared first on TWZ .
detail: Lockheed Martin is developing the PAC-3 Edge, an advanced interceptor for the Patriot missile defense system, promising significantly enhanced range, altitude, and maneuverability. This upgrade is crucial because the Patriot system is a foundational air defense asset for numerous countries, and its capabilities must continuously evolve to counter rapidly developing aerial threats. The PAC-3 Edge is designed to address sophisticated ballistic and cruise missiles, and potentially emerging hypersonic weapons, by improving its 'hit-to-kill' precision and engagement envelope. This modernization effort ensures the Patriot system remains effective against increasingly complex and agile threats, maintaining a critical layer of defense in a dynamic global security landscape where adversaries are constantly advancing their missile technologies.

title: New Coyote Anti-Drone Interceptor Swaps Jet Engine For Rocket Power
summary: The Coyote Block 2 is already combat proven, but more capable kamikaze drones have driven a need to fly faster and farther. The post New Coyote Anti-Drone Interceptor Swaps Jet Engine For Rocket Power appeared first on TWZ .
detail: The Coyote anti-drone interceptor, specifically the Block 2 variant, is being re-engineered to utilize rocket power instead of its current jet engine. This significant design change is a direct response to the proliferation of faster and more capable kamikaze drones, which pose an increasing threat in modern conflicts. Rocket propulsion offers rapid acceleration and higher top speeds, which are essential for effectively intercepting and neutralizing agile, high-speed drone targets. This enhancement allows the Coyote to engage threats more quickly and potentially at greater distances, improving its overall effectiveness in countering the evolving spectrum of unmanned aerial system (UAS) threats. The shift underscores the urgent need for air defense systems to adapt to the rapid advancements in drone technology.

title: Powerus unveils fully autonomous drone interceptors
summary: Once a threat is detected, the new Guardian 3 interceptors are immediately launched toward it. They strike using advanced AI and navigational systems.
detail: Powerus has unveiled its Guardian 3 interceptors, which are fully autonomous drone defense systems. These interceptors are designed to detect aerial threats independently and launch themselves without human intervention, utilizing advanced AI and navigational systems to engage targets. This development is significant as it represents a major step towards automated air defense against drones, reducing response times and operational workload for human operators. Full autonomy allows for quicker decision-making and engagement, which is critical for countering drone swarms or rapid, coordinated attacks. It offers a scalable and efficient solution to the growing challenge posed by the widespread use of drones, from small commercial models to larger military UAVs, by enabling continuous, high-speed defense operations.

title: One user interface, multiple autonomous systems: Forterra debuts OASIS-OneLink technology
summary: Forterra introduced its new OASIS-OneLink platform that allows operators and service members to control autonomous systems using a single user interface.
detail: Forterra has introduced OASIS-OneLink, a new technology platform designed to allow operators to control multiple autonomous systems, such as ground robots and aerial drones, through a single, unified user interface. This innovation is crucial for modern military operations, where the increasing deployment of diverse autonomous assets can lead to operator overload and inefficient command structures. By consolidating control into one interface, OASIS-OneLink simplifies the management of complex robotic forces, reduces cognitive load on operators, and enables better coordination and integration of various unmanned systems. This 'system of systems' approach is vital for maximizing the potential of human-machine teaming and enhancing operational effectiveness in multi-domain warfare scenarios.

title: AGVs vs. UGVs: A new class of ground autonomy takes the field
summary: [Sponsored] One commander, many robots: Fully autonomous ground vehicles are reshaping the battlefield.
detail: The article highlights the emergence of 'fully autonomous ground vehicles' (AGVs) on the battlefield, distinguishing them from traditional 'unmanned ground vehicles' (UGVs). While UGVs are typically remotely operated or semi-autonomous, AGVs possess the capability to perform complex tasks and make decisions independently. This distinction is critical because AGVs are poised to revolutionize ground warfare by enabling a single commander to manage multiple robotic assets, thereby increasing force projection and reducing human risk in dangerous environments. This new class of ground autonomy signifies a shift towards more sophisticated robotic integration, allowing for enhanced efficiency, faster operational tempo, and the ability to delegate dull, dirty, and dangerous tasks to machines, freeing human soldiers for more complex roles.
